chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Saeed ibn Qays al-Hamdani, who said:

I looked one day in the war to a man upon whom were two garments, so I moved my horse and behold it was the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So I said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, in the likes of this (garment) in this place?' He said, 'Yes, O Saeed ibn Qays! There is not a servant except that he has from Allah a guardian and a protector, with him two angels who protect him from falling from the top of a mountain or falling into a well. So when the Decree descends, they leave him alone and with everything.'
ai.seo_question: What is the role of angels in protecting humans from accidental death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Abu Hamza al-Thumali from Sa'id ibn Qays al-Hamdani, highlights the Shia theological distinction between general divine protection (hafizah) and specific fatal decree (qada). It illustrates that while angels guard humans from accidental or premature death, they release their hold only when the predetermined time of death arrives, underscoring the balance between divine will and human agency.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Saeed Bin Qays Al Hamdany who said,

‘During the war, I looked at a man upon whom were two clothes. So I moved my horse and it was Amir Al-Momineenasws. So I said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! In the likes of this (clothes) in this place?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes, O Saeed Bin Qays! There is none from a servant except that there is for him, from Allahazwj, a protector, and two Angels are Allocated to be with him protecting him from him falling from the top of a mountain, or falling into a well. So when the Ordainment descends, they both leave him alone and between everything’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd ibn Sinan from abu Hamza from Sa’id ibn Qays al- Hamadani who has said the following:

“One day during a war I looked on a man who was wearing two pieces of garment on him. I moved my horse nearer to him and I found him to be Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) and I said, ‘O Amir al-Mu’minin, is this a place (to be in with just two pieces of garment and no coats of arms)?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, O Sa’id ibn al-Qays. For every servant of Allah there is a guard from Allah and a protecting angel to see that he will not fall off of a cliff or into a well, but when the appointed time comes for his death the angels just leave him alone to his own self.’”
